scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #7103: This is the Location C office. None of our machines
(PC11 to PC14) can reach anything at all any more -- not the other sites,
and the word here is that we cannot even reach "our own gateway". I won't
pretend to know what a gateway is, but everything times out for all of us
at once and we have not touched a thing in this office. Location C has been
cut off on your side. Find out why and reconnect us today; an entire office
is down.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. Location C's gateway (router4 LAN interface,
  192.168.200.1) is up; PC11-PC14 reach it with 0% loss; and Location C exchanges
  traffic with the rest of the network over the RIP core -- Location A reaches
  Location C (PC4 -> 192.168.100.1 and the 192.168.200.0/24 hosts) with 0% loss,
  so the inter-site path is forwarding in both directions. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a total Location C
  isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Location C totally cut off
from its gateway and the rest of the network -- is NOT reproducible: PC11 reaches
its gateway 192.168.200.1 (router4 LAN) with 0% loss, and the inter-site path is
up (Location A's PC4 reaches 192.168.100.1 and the 192.168.200.0/24 Location C
hosts with 0% loss), so Location C is exchanging traffic across the RIP core.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: Location C's gateway and its inter-site
connectivity are healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct
agent reproduces the claimed failures -- PC11 -> gateway and a cross-site path
(e.g. PC4 <-> Location C) -- finds them working, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" an isolated Location C, a downed router4, or a severed RIP link to
satisfy the "totally cut off" ticket is over-diagnosing.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC11-PC14 reach gateway 192.168.200.1 and Location A reaches Location C across the RIP core with 0% loss at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The nftables/iptables FORWARD chain on router6, specifically a set of DROP rules applied to traffic ingressing on `eth2` (the r6_r3 uplink connecting router6 to the rest of the routing mesh via router3).

**Mechanism:** Router6 sits at the boundary of the 172.18.51.0/24 zone (PC15–PC18, switch10, mswitch2). Its eth2 is the sole uplink to the wider network. The FORWARD chain contains a near-total block: one narrow ACCEPT for HTTP from 172.16.10.0/24 to 172.18.51.1, followed by DROP rules for TCP, UDP, and a final catch-all DROP for any remaining protocol. Every packet relayed from router3 into the 172.18.51.x zone — including ICMP — is dropped at the catch-all (28 drops confirmed at inspection time). Return traffic suffers the same fate: replies from PC11 to PC15 travel PC11→router4→router3→router6 eth2 and are also caught by the DROP rule, making pings bidirectionally fail.

**Localization:** router6, nftables `table ip filter` → `chain FORWARD`, rules matching `iifname "eth2"` with drop verdicts. Router6's eth1 carries `172.18.51.254/24` and can itself reach PC16 with 0% loss, confirming L2 and the mswitch2 bridge (br_vlan51) are healthy — the block is purely on forwarded transit traffic.

**Root cause:** An nftables ACL on router6 drops all forwarded packets arriving from the r6_r3 uplink (eth2), completely severing the 172.18.51.x subnet from every other site in the network.

**Fix:** Remove the three DROP rules from router6's FORWARD chain (`nft delete rule ip filter FORWARD <handle>` for each drop rule, or `iptables -D FORWARD -i eth2 -j DROP` etc.). Retain or discard the narrow HTTP ACCEPT rule per policy intent.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC11-PC14 reach gateway 192.168.200.1 and Location A reaches Location C across the RIP core with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report does not record the baseline connectivity checks (PC11–PC14 to 192.168.200.1 and Location A to Location C at 0% loss); it instead diagnoses a router6 FORWARD DROP rule.

The agent's investigation logs show targeted probes (pings), routing and interface inspections, and firewall listing commands; the writeup's claims mostly follow from those observations though the explicit nft rule text/counters are truncated in the log. Overall the reasoning is coherent and the conclusion is well-supported by the observed failures and routing/interface state.
